Subject: Sizing ask for isolated inference lanes (HealthCore pilot)

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security and infra teams want a clear sizing recommendation for two paths before we move a pilot to procurement: 1) private (VPC + customer-controlled airgap later) and 2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool).

Key constraints:
- Regulated PHI workload, residency in us-east-1 preferred.
- Expected peak: ~1200 concurrent inference sessions at 256-token average (mostly chat completion reranks).
- Daily burst variance: 2x on weekdays, 0.5x weekend baseline.
- SLA: p95 latency target <= 200ms for interactive paths.
- Audit + retention: 90-day request logs, encrypted with our KMS.

Could you send a short recommendation (node counts, GPU type mix, and an ops play for burst/fallback) so we can size budget for procurement? Also attach your filled security questionnaire (we sent ours).

Best,
Samira
Sr. Product Ops — HealthCore

Priya / Marissa —

Quick recommendations (keeping the ask tight):

1) Pilot (30–60 day, prove performance + compliance):
- Private path: 3 x H100-80GB (or equivalent multi-GPU partitioning) in dedicated VPC with 1:1 tenancy; these give ample memory for large chat models, support KV cache hot-warm optimization.
- Dedicated path: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent in Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved short-term) + 1 burst node (H100) to handle weekday spikes.

Rationale: H100s for Private because customers often bring heavier context windows and need lower tail latency under KV cache pressure. A100s are cost-efficient in Dedicated with predictable throughput. One burst H100 node avoids cold starts.

Sizing maths (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline concurrency 1200 sessions * 256 tokens avg = ~307k tokens in-flight; with batching and prefix caching expect effective concurrent GPU contexts ~120–180 depending on model and batching window.
- For interactive p95 <=200ms we assume 8–10 seq/sec per H100-equivalent on large chat models; safe pilot: 3 H100s => comfortable margin.
- Production commit: recommend 8 x H100-equivalent private nodes OR 12 x A100-equivalent reserved for Dedicated (with 2x H100 bursts). This gives headroom for 2.5x daily bursts and sustained throughput.

2) Burst / fallback plan:
- Configure automatic routing policy: Dedicated -> Private -> Hosted compatible model variant. During capacity strain, route non-critical rerank jobs to quantized/reserved-hosted model (L4/L4-like) with degraded latency expectations.
- Enable prefix & KV cache pinning for common contexts; reduces token work by ~30% in our measurements.

3) Compliance / ops notes:
- KMS integration: support BYOK/HSM; Private is straightforward; Dedicated supports per-tenant CMKs with RBAC for key usage.
- Audit: enable 90-day request logs retention in S3 with access logs and token-level tracing. Estimate ~60GB/day of compressed logs for their concurrency (confirm retention calc).

4) Commercial framing:
- Private: one-time onboarding + monthly platform fee. Suggest framing as 3-month pilot on private (cover onboarding), then convert to 12-mo term if they want production SLA.
- Dedicated: lower onboarding, higher committed monthly fee; propose 12-mo committed plan with 1-month ramp credit for pilot.

Next steps: I can draft the node counts/price math if you want — need their expected QPS distribution (hourly) and token mix (inference vs embeddings).

— Karthik
Senior Deal Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing ask for isolated inference lanes (HealthCore pilot)

Hi Samira —

Thanks — we reviewed and sketched two pragmatic options and an ops playbook. High-level summary (attached is a one-pager version of Karthik's notes plus our proposal draft):

Option A — Private (recommended for strict PHI + long-term residency):
- Pilot: 3 x H100-80GB in your VPC (Redwood-managed private control plane), KMS BYOK, 90-day logs to your S3.
- Production: scale to 8 x H100-equivalent nodes.
- Pros: lowest tail latency, easiest KMS/HSM integration, clear audit trail.
- Cons: higher onboarding and capex-ish feel; longer lead time (~4–6 weeks to provision depending on procurement).

Option B — Redwood Dedicated (faster time-to-RUN):
- Pilot: 4 x A100-80GB reserved in our Dedicated pool + 1 burst H100 node for weekday peaks.
- Production: 12 x A100-equivalent reserved; auto-burst to 2 H100 nodes for spikes.
- Pros: faster procurement (weeks), lower onboarding, predictable monthly commit.
- Cons: slightly higher p95 in worst-case payloads vs Private; KMS integration is per-tenant via Redwood-managed keys unless customer brings CMK (we can scope).

Ops / fallback:
- Routing policy: Primary path = Dedicated/Private (per selection), fallback = Redwood-hosted quantized model (L4-like) for non-SLA critical batch reranks.
- Enable prefix/KV caching and request-level tracing; this reduces effective load by ~20–35% depending on prompt reuse.

Commercial ask: would you be open to a 3-month paid pilot on the selected path with an option to convert to a 12-month commitment? If yes, well include onboarding and a locked provisioning window in the SOW.

Can we set a 30-minute call this week to walk through the tradeoffs and procurement runway? Karthik / Marissa will join. Proposed times: Thu 6/3 10:00–10:30am ET or Fri 6/4 2:00–2:30pm ET.

I attached the draft proposal and our filled security questionnaire for your review.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
